chosen.premise: Paras’s mushrooms control it, ordering the bug to extract juice from tree trunks.
chosen.hook: The mushrooms on Paras’s back are giving the orders.
chosen.visualIdea: Reveal tree-root burrowing first, then animate the mushrooms controlling Paras like a puppet.
chosen.note: The control reversal is unusually concrete and strongly supported by multiple entries; the puppet-like visual gives it an excellent reveal.

candidates.premise: The mushrooms draining Paras’s body are also valuable: dried tochukaso can make medicine for extending life.
candidates.hook: Paras’s nutrient-stealing mushrooms are prized as life-extending medicine.
candidates.visualIdea: Contrast Paras weakening beneath the mushrooms with tochukaso being dried, powdered, and used as medicine.
candidates.note: Excellent contradiction between exploitation and life-extending medicine; the claim that Paras itself is weakened is implied rather than directly stated.

candidates.premise: In Alola, Paras’s mushrooms fail to grow properly because of insufficient moisture or nutrients.
candidates.hook: In Alola, Paras’s famous mushrooms don’t grow right.
candidates.visualIdea: Compare a large, healthy tochukaso-covered Paras with an Alolan Paras whose mushrooms are stunted.
candidates.note: Specific and visually comparative, but the Alola detail is less inherently dramatic and the cause remains an either-or possibility.

candidates.premise: Paras’s back mushrooms are parasites: they grow by stealing nutrients from the Bug Pokémon carrying them.
candidates.hook: Paras isn’t carrying mushrooms—the mushrooms are feeding on Paras.
candidates.visualIdea: Show nutrients flowing from Paras into the mushrooms while the mushrooms visibly enlarge.
candidates.note: A strong Paras-specific premise with clear nutrient-drain imagery, though the basic parasite relationship is already fairly familiar.

candidates.premise: Paras is born without its signature mushrooms; they only emerge as its body matures.
candidates.hook: Baby Paras has no mushrooms on its back.
candidates.visualIdea: Morph an infant Paras with a bare back into a mature Paras covered in tochukaso.
candidates.note: A clean developmental fact with an obvious before-and-after visual, but less dramatic than the control premise.

candidates.premise: No matter how much Paras eats, its mushrooms steal most of the nutrition before Paras can use it.
candidates.hook: Paras can eat endlessly and still lose most of the nutrition.
candidates.visualIdea: Show food entering Paras, then split the nutrients so most flow upward into the mushrooms.
candidates.note: The contradiction is compelling and well supported, although 'eat endlessly' slightly overstates the cited wording.

rounds.request: None—the chosen angle is strong enough. Even stronger execution would clarify that the Pokédex explicitly describes both commanding and controlling, rather than presenting the puppet imagery as literal animation.
